description: Request settings of the hosted Qwen3.5-9B pin of the Study 2 test round (ADDENDUM_study2.md, S2-A11), given to `athena2_s2.py` with `--pins ../models/model_pins_s2_or.json --model-pin qwen35_9b_or_s2`. The "embeddings" section is a copy of that of model_pins_s2.json (the SHA-256 of each entry is the same), so a run records the same embedding pin hash and reads the same query embeddings.

qwen35_9b_or_s2.route: OpenRouter, provider locked to DeepInfra at bf16 (no fallback)

identity.vendor_model_id: Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B (open weights, Apache-2.0, post-trained; thinking is on by default)
identity.note: The same open weights as qwen35_9b_s2, served by a hosted provider at bf16 instead of the local 8-bit GGUF (UD-Q8_K_XL). The provider does not state which weight revision it serves and sends no system fingerprint. Thinking is turned off with the OpenRouter reasoning parameter instead of the chat-template argument of the local server. DeepInfra is chosen among the three bf16 endpoints for its stated quantization, uptime and support of every parameter sent; if it becomes unavailable during the run, the replacement provider is reported.

study2.replaces: qwen35_9b_s2 in the test round (ADDENDUM_study2.md, S2-A11)
study2.change: same request settings (temperature 0.2, max_tokens 8192, thinking off); hosted bf16 deployment instead of the local llama-server

qwen3_embedding_06b.panel_name: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (embedding model of the dense retrieval condition)
qwen3_embedding_06b.route: local llama-server in embedding mode on the lab Windows machine, reached through an SSH tunnel; the address is read from $ATHENA_EMBED_BASE_URL and is not part of the pin

request.query_template:
Instruct: Given an identifier and the code around it, retrieve the passages of the coding standard that apply to it
Query:{query}

identity.llama_cpp_build: version 0.6.0-dev (build 11433, commit 50569eb87), built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64
identity.note: Queries are embedded with the instruction of query_template and passages without one, as the model card prescribes; the instruction is fixed here and is not tuned. Vectors are L2-normalised by the harness and compared by dot product. gguf_sha256_listed is the LFS hash shown by the repository at the pinned revision; gguf_sha256_local, computed on the serving machine, matches it. A different llama.cpp build or server command is a different deployment.
